description: EvalCI question category definitions. Each category groups related evaluation questions to enable fine-grained regression detection. The Regression Fingerprinter analyses score changes at the category level to identify which *type* of capability regressed.

categories.description: Closed-domain factual questions with unambiguous answers. Tests whether the RAG system retrieves and restates documented facts accurately.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: A drop in this category primarily signals retriever failure — the relevant factual chunks are not being fetched.

categories.description: Questions requiring chaining multiple facts or computation steps. Tests the generator's ability to synthesise across multiple retrieved chunks.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: A drop in this category, especially with stable grounding, primarily signals generator failure — the model fails to chain reasoning across multiple contexts.

categories.description: Questions asking for precise definitions of technical or domain-specific terms. Tests exact retrieval of definitional passages.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Regressions here often indicate chunking issues where definitions are split across chunk boundaries (retriever failure).

categories.description: Questions about cause-and-effect relationships in the domain. Tests whether the RAG system can retrieve mechanistic explanations accurately.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Drops here with low grounding suggest retriever failure; drops with high grounding suggest generator hallucination.

categories.description: Step-by-step how-to questions. Tests whether the RAG system can assemble ordered procedural information from multiple chunks.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Step omissions or ordering errors with high grounding indicate generator failures in synthesis.

categories.description: Questions requiring side-by-side comparison of two or more concepts. Tests multi-document retrieval and synthesis.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Low context_recall paired with low correctness strongly implicates retriever failure (missing one of the compared concepts).

categories.description: Diagnostic questions presenting a symptom and asking for root causes. Tests the system's ability to retrieve and reason over technical failure scenarios.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Regressions here are often generator failures — the model proposes plausible-sounding but incorrect diagnoses.

categories.description: Questions about system design rationale and architectural trade-offs. Tests conceptual retrieval and nuanced synthesis.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: High hallucination_risk with moderate correctness suggests the generator is mixing parametric bias with retrieved context.

categories.description: Questions about specific code patterns, APIs, and library behaviours. Tests retrieval of technical documentation and code comments.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Regressions here often indicate embedding model issues with code-heavy text (retriever failure).

categories.description: Questions about risks, biases, and safety considerations. Tests nuanced retrieval of cautionary and compliance-related content.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Low scores here are a red flag — both retriever completeness and generator conservatism are critical for safety-adjacent answers.

categories.description: Questions about deploying, configuring, and operating the system in production. Tests operational documentation retrieval.
categories.primary_failure_indicator: Regressions here typically signal gaps in operational documentation coverage in the vector store.
